about.title: Napa Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Napa is compact enough that most residents drive the same handful of streets every day: Jefferson Street to the store, Soscol Avenue toward the outlets, 1st Street into downtown, or Route 29 on the way in and out of the valley. Those same corridors also appear most often in the city's public collision records. For 2025, the final count for Napa came to 253 injury collisions, 357 people hurt, and 3 traffic deaths, with reports clustering on Thursday afternoons between 4 and 6 p.m. Behind each entry is a person sorting out what comes next: a rental car, a missed shift at a winery or the hospital, a stack of bills with no clear sender. LawProactive exists to make one piece of that simpler. We are not a law firm. We are a free service that connects you with an independent personal injury attorney who handles Napa County car accident claims on contingency, meaning no fee unless your case recovers money. You talk with someone who knows California's rules, and we step aside.

items.title: The clock matters in California
items.desc: Most car accident claims here must be filed within two years, but if a city, county, or state vehicle was involved, a claim may need to be filed in as little as six months. An attorney can sort out which deadline applies to your Napa crash before it becomes a problem.

items.title: Being partly at fault doesn't end your claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you shared some blame at that Soscol Avenue intersection, you may still recover damages reduced by your share. The attorney's job is to keep the other side from exaggerating your portion.

items.title: No recorded statement, no upfront cost
items.desc: The other driver's insurer will likely call asking for a recorded account; you are not required to give one, and an attorney can handle that conversation. Attorneys in our network work on contingency and there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: I was hit on Route 29 heading into Napa. Does it matter that it's a state highway?
items.answer: It can. If the crash involved only private drivers, the usual two-year deadline applies. But if road conditions or a government vehicle played a role, a claim against a public entity may have to be filed within six months, which is why speaking to an attorney early is worth it.

items.question: What should I do in the first few days after a Napa car accident?
items.answer: Get checked by a doctor even if you feel mostly fine, since neck and back injuries often surface later. Save photos, the police report number, witness names, and any dashcam footage, and avoid giving the other insurer a recorded statement until you have spoken with an attorney.

items.question: Is there a cap on what I can recover for pain and suffering in California?
items.answer: For a standard car accident claim, California does not cap non-economic damages such as pain, suffering, or loss of enjoyment of life. The amount depends on the specific facts of your injury and recovery, and no one can promise a particular result. An attorney can explain how those damages are typically documented.
